correctness.rationale: The full proof gives a bijection from the constrained pairs (t,e) to multisets of rooted colored functional components; t^3=t restricts each component to a fixed star or a decorated 2-cycle. An exact square-lift construction characterizes nonessential rank-two pairs; one extra fixed center per e-fiber is the sharp boundary. The resulting fiber generating functions and multiset transforms yield r_3 and r_2 for arbitrary n. The n>=5 monoid generator reduction and product rule are explicitly imported and credited from Gould–Grau–Johnson. The independent standard-library direct orbit and Burnside checks at n<=6, including the n=5,6 counts (15,17) and (46,37), corroborate the theorem without claiming finite evidence proves the infinite identity. The n=4 exception is excluded.

originality.rationale: Gould–Grau–Johnson (arXiv:2307.11596v1, Sections 2, 4 and 8) classify the singular endomorphisms and prove that the minimum generating rank reduces to two unit-conjugacy orbit counts, while explicitly leaving those counts as an enumeration problem. The present functional-component and square-lift arguments provide both counts for all n >= 5. The numerical rank-two sequence is not new as a string of integers (OEIS A097391), and the classical plane-partition product is credited. No accessible prior work was identified that proves the End(T_n) essential-orbit interpretation together with the rank-three orbit formula and resulting exact minimal generator rank. Priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: An unidentified post-2023 paper or thesis could answer the same exact enumeration problem; negative searches cannot establish uniqueness.
The 1998 primary full text and the related 2023 dissertation were not materially accessible; their complete coverage was not certified.
The rank-two integer sequence itself is previously recorded as OEIS A097391; only its algebraic interpretation and combination with rank-three enumeration are asserted original.
Finite verification covers conjugacy orbits only to n=6 and does not replace the all-degree proof.

value.rationale: The motivating published paper explicitly poses enumeration of precisely these two orbit terms as a route to the minimum number of generators of a natural finite endomorphism monoid. Both exact terms are now evaluated for all n>=5, and their sum gives an immediately computable invariant across every degree. The two-cycle multiset term and the nontrivial square-lift essentiality characterization are structural, not arbitrary tabulations. The numerical coincidence with already-known plane-partition sequence is appropriately credited and the added algebraic meaning is mathematically motivated.
